information: remindit-app-pwa store-layer tests must import submodules directly (e.g. @/stores/catalog) NOT the @/stores barrel, because the barrel runs initStores + a dev logger as a side effect. happy-dom is the global testEnvironment (see rstest.config.ts), so crypto.randomUUID() and localStorage are available. Use `import { resetStores } from "../fixtures/reset"` + beforeEach(resetStores) to clear all stores/localStorage between tests. removeCatalogItem cascades to drop referencing $list entries via removeListEntriesForItem but deliberately does NOT write $history.

vp migrate (v0.2.9, --no-interactive --no-hooks) on a Vite 8 + React + Bun project auto-migrates ESLint→Oxlint AND Prettier→Oxfmt even WITHOUT --full: it deletes eslint.config.js and .prettierrc, removes eslint/prettier/typescript-eslint/prettier-plugin-tailwindcss devDeps, rewrites lint/format scripts to "vp lint ."/"vp fmt", injects huge lint{}+fmt{} blocks into vite.config.ts, and ALSO rewrites /* eslint-disable */ comments in src files (found in theme-provider.tsx). To defer the lint/fmt migration while keeping core Vite+: git checkout -- eslint.config.js .prettierrc and any touched src files, restore lint/format scripts + eslint/prettier devDeps in package.json, strip lint{}/fmt{} from vite.config.ts keeping defineConfig/lazyPlugins from vite-plus, then bun install. Verified working after: build (tsc -b && vp build), eslint, vp dev smoke test all pass. Generated fmt block also contained a cosmetic duplicate "pnpm-lock.yaml" ignorePatterns entry.

In the remindit-app-pwa swarm, the `swarm-worker` subagent type frequently returned its turn prematurely (after only the hivemind/swarmmail init steps) instead of completing the task, especially for code-writing subtasks. The `general` subagent type reliably executes multi-step code+test work to completion. LESSON: for implementation subtasks in this project, prefer spawning `general` agents over `swarm-worker`, or tightly constrain the prompt to a single deliverable. Also: Ark UI Listbox with `selectionMode="none"` still forwards the user `onClick` (zag-js merges handlers via mergeProps), so store-driven click handlers work without enabling internal selection.

RemindIt PWA (Rsbuild + React 19 + Tailwind v4) theme architecture: the dark palette is ALREADY fully wired via Tailwind v4's `.dark` class — `@custom-variant dark (&:is(.dark *));` in src/styles/globals.css plus a `.dark { ... }` token override block. To enable dark mode you only need to apply `.dark` to <html>. Light is the default `:root` token set. State layer is Nanostores (`@nanostores/persistent`); `persistentAtom<"light"|"dark"|"system">("remindit:theme", "system")` + an initTheme() side-effect (toggle .dark class, subscribe to store, listen to matchMedia for "system") is the proven pattern. A separate accent-color system lives in src/styles/theme.css (`.theme-*` classes) — do NOT touch it for light/dark work. NOTE: `bun run lint` fails project-wide on pre-existing `noDuplicateCustomProperties` warnings in that theme.css; unrelated to theme-toggle work.

In remindit-pwa (Vite+ React19+TS+Tailwind v4), migrating from Vite+ Oxlint/Oxfmt to Biome succeeded on 2026-08-21: `bun add -d @biomejs/biome` installed 2.5.10. package.json script mapping: `lint` -> `biome check .` (was `vp lint .`), `format` -> `biome format --write .` (was `vp fmt "**/*.{ts,tsx}"`), and new `lint:ci` -> `biome ci .`. Biome `ci` command EXISTS (runs check without writing, fails on any diff). dev/build/preview/typecheck stay on `vp`. biome.json uses `files.includes` negated globs (v2 has NO `files.ignore`), `javascript.formatter.semicolons: asNeeded` (NOT `formatter.semicolons`), `assist.actions.source.organizeImports: on` for import sort, and `useSortedClasses` linter rule for Tailwind sorting. Do NOT run full codebase reformat during install; another worker handles that.

When removing Payload CMS collections from the hct-themed monorepo: shared/types/payload-types.ts and admin/src/app/(payload)/admin/importMap.js are GENERATED files, so editing them by hand is wrong. Run `bun run generate:types` then `bun run generate:importmap` in the admin workspace; importmap may report 'No new imports found, skipping writing import map' when removals don't add imports, which is fine. Also note Media collection 'kind' radio option value 'projects' must be kept even when the projects collection is deleted, because web /case-studies and 62 media rows depend on it. Lint for the admin workspace: `bun run lint` (0 errors expected; pre-existing warnings in seed/, tests, Copy.tsx are unrelated). Web check: `bun run astro-check`.

In remindit-app-pwa (Rsbuild + Rstest), store unit tests must import the store submodule directly (e.g. '@/stores/selectors') NOT the '@/stores' barrel — the barrel runs initStores() which seeds from seed JSON and randomizes user defaults, polluting tests. Also `vi` is NOT an auto-injected global here; use only imports from '@rstest/core'. Reset persistentJSON stores between cases with $store.set([...]) because they read/write localStorage (happy-dom) and cache values.

In remindit-app-pwa (Rsbuild/Rstest PWA), `$history` is exported from `@/stores/history`, NOT `@/stores/list` — even though `addToList`/`removeFromList` live in list.ts and are the only writers of history. Store tests must import each submodule directly (`@/stores/history`, `@/stores/list`, `@/stores/catalog`, `@/stores/categories`) and never the `@/stores` barrel, because the barrel runs `initStores` + a dev logger as a side effect. Rstest CLI uses POSITIONAL filters (`bun run test tests/stores/integration.test.ts`), not `--filter` (which errors). happy-dom is the global test env (rstest.config.ts). `buildSeedData()` and `shoppingHistory3mo` both call `generateShoppingHistory` with fresh `Date.now()`, so they are separate array instances — assert against `shoppingHistory3mo` directly, never by reference equality.

In the remindit-app-pwa project the web app manifest is NOT a static file — it is generated inline from rsbuild.config.ts via pluginPWA({ dev:true, webAppManifest:{ content:{...} } }). Editing public/manifest.webmanifest or public/manifest.json has NO effect (those files don't exist; the inline config wins). Icon PNGs/SVGs live in public/ and are copied into dist/ at build time. pluginPWA also injects <link rel="manifest"> and <script src="/register-sw.js"> into the served HTML automatically. Dev server runs on port 3000 (Rsbuild default), not 5173.

In the remindit-app-pwa project, tests/stores/* test files import store submodules directly (e.g. @/stores/categories) NOT the @/stores barrel, because the barrel runs initStores + a dev logger side effect. resetStores (tests/fixtures/reset) clears $categories to [] and does NOT seed UNCATEGORIZED_ID, so any test asserting the UNCATEGORIZED_ID sentinel's presence must seed it manually (e.g. $categories.set([{ id: UNCATEGORIZED_ID, name: 'Uncategorized' }])). happy-dom is global, so crypto.randomUUID() and localStorage work without setup. Use `beforeEach(resetStores)`.

In remindit-app-pwa, the list store's `removeFromList(id)` removes a list entry and expects the ENTRY id (ListEntry.id / SelectedViewEntry.entryId), NOT the catalog item id. Clicking a catalog item to remove it must resolve itemId -> entryId first (e.g. via $selectedView.find(e => e.itemId === item.id)). Confusingly, `addToList(itemId)` DOES take the item id. Gotcha when wiring toggle-off behavior in ItemsPanel. Also: Ark UI Accordion content stays in the DOM but is `hidden` until opened; in rstest query item buttons with `getByRole("button", { name, hidden: true })` and click via `fireEvent` (which dispatches on hidden nodes).

In this project (RemindIt PWA, Ark UI ToggleGroup), the underlying zag-js toggle-group always treats `value` as `string[]` and `onValueChange` returns `details.value: string[]` — even in single-select mode. To make a single-selection segmented control (e.g. ThemeToggle), pass `multiple={false}` AND `deselectable={false}` (deselectable defaults true and is ignored only when multiple=true), set `value={[current]}` and read `details.value[0]`. Do NOT pass a `type="single"` prop — zag-js/Ark props have no `type` field and it type-errors as an invalid div attribute.

In Ark UI (@ark-ui/react) Listbox, you CAN attach a user onClick to <ListboxItem> even with selectionMode="none". The internal getItemProps onClick (zag-js) is merged with the user handler via mergeProps, so both fire; the machine's ITEM.CLICK for selectionMode="none" ignores selection but does not call preventDefault on the React click event, so the user onClick runs. This is the correct pattern for "row = action (e.g. remove)" lists where items aren't meant to be selectable. Verified with an Rstest + Testing Library test in the remindit-app-pwa project.

In this Rsbuild + Rstest project, tsconfig.json `compilerOptions.paths` aliases (e.g. a `seed` alias → `./seed`) ARE resolved by Rstest at test runtime, but Rsbuild's bundler only applies the `@`→`./src` alias. Consequence: app (src) code importing repo-root modules should use relative paths (e.g. `../../seed/items_categories.json`) or add an `alias` entry in rsbuild.config.ts; tests can safely use the tsconfig path alias. When relocating a JSON data file, remember to repoint both the app importer and tests.

remindit-pwa Vite+ migration verified clean (branch feat/vite-plus-migration, commit 2557f3e): commit only touches package.json/vite.config.ts/bun.lock; src/ has zero diff vs main and no oxlint/oxfmt comment remnants. Gotchas found during verification: (1) `vp dev` silently falls back to port 5174 if an orphaned dev server holds 5173 - check `lsof -nP -iTCP:5173` and kill stale node processes (cwd confirms ownership) before smoke testing; (2) killing the `bun run dev`/`vp dev` wrapper does NOT kill the underlying vite-plus-core node CLI process - kill that PID directly; (3) `vp build` output is fast (~266ms) but does not typecheck, so `tsc -b && vp build` in the build script is load-bearing.

RESEARCH 1/4 - vite+ and vp migrate for remindit-pwa (Vite 8, React 19, bun, Tailwind v4 CSS-first, Shark/Ark UI). vp CLI v0.2.9 global. Researched 2026-08-21 from viteplus.dev docs + CLI help.

WHAT VITE+ IS: VoidZero unified toolchain = global CLI vp plus local package vite-plus. Bundles Vite 8 (Rolldown default), Vitest 4.x re-exported as vite-plus/test*, Oxlint, Oxfmt, tsdown, Vite Task. Manages node runtime (opt out: vp env off), delegates package management to packageManager field in package.json (bun here). Core alias: vite resolves to npm:@voidzero-dev/vite-plus-core via overrides. vite-plus exports only defineConfig, defineProject, lazyPlugins; all other vite imports keep working through the alias.

vp migrate FILES TOUCHED: package.json gets pinned vite-plus devDependency at the concrete CLI version. Standalone bun projects (no workspaces) get concrete specs and no catalogs because bun catalogs need a workspaces root. Keeps/adds a direct vite dependency plus overrides: vite -> npm:@voidzero-dev/vite-plus-core. Bun-specific rule: the core alias is mirrored as a direct vite dep so Bun resolves the peer provider before applying overrides.

In the remindit-app-pwa project (React 19 + Rsbuild + Rstest, happy-dom env), `vi` is NOT a static export of `@rstest/core` and is NOT auto-injected as a global (rstest.config.ts has `globals` off). There is a `@rstest/core/globals` subpath but it only provides TYPE declarations. So mocks must be plain functions and you cannot use `vi.resetModules()`/`vi.fn()` — work around module-level guards by leveraging the code's own subscriptions (e.g. initTheme() subscribes to the store, so re-applying happens on every store.set without re-calling initTheme). Also `@nanostores/persistent` `persistentAtom` stores values as RAW strings in localStorage here (NOT JSON-encoded), so assert `localStorage.getItem(key)` equals the raw value directly. Finally, tsconfig `include` covers `src`, so test files placed under `src/` ARE typechecked — avoid jest-dom matcher types (use standard `expect(x).toBe(...)` / `getAttribute`) to keep typecheck green.

In the remindit-app-pwa project (Rsbuild + rsbuild-plugin-pwa), favicons v7 (itgalaxy/favicons, JS API only) is used to generate PWA assets via scripts/generate-favicons.ts. Key gotchas: (1) There is NO `manifest: false` config option in favicons v7 — to avoid emitting a manifest.webmanifest that conflicts with the Rsbuild-plugin-pwa-generated dist/manifest.webmanifest (which is built from the inline webAppManifest in rsbuild.config.ts), filter out the 'manifest.webmanifest' entry from the `files` array before writing. (2) Two master sources are used: normal SVG (public/remindit-icon.svg) as the main `source`, and the maskable-safe SVG (public/remindit-icon-maskable.svg) passed via `manifestMaskable` to produce 9 maskable android-chrome PNGs alongside the 9 standard (purpose "any"). (3) favicons can TRANSIENTLY drop the favicons-platform images (favicon.ico/16/32/48x) on a first run (likely a sharp worker race) — simply re-running the script generates them correctly. Always verify favicon-*.png exist after a run. (4) `bun run format` (biome --write) reformats the WHOLE repo including unrelated files; revert unrelated changes with `git checkout` to respect scope. favicons v7 needs no @types/bun — use node:fs/promises writeFile, not Bun.write, to avoid TS errors.

In Rstest (@rstest/core), the config key for the test environment is `testEnvironment` (e.g. testEnvironment: 'happy-dom'), NOT `environment`. Using `environment` causes a TS error: "Object literal may only specify known properties, and 'environment' does not exist in type 'RstestConfigExport'". happy-dom must be installed as a devDependency. Setting it globally is fine and also works for React/Testing Library smoke tests.

RESEARCH 2/4 - vp migrate exact behavior for remindit-pwa. Scripts rewritten preserving args: dev "vite" becomes "vp dev"; build "tsc -b && vite build" becomes "tsc -b && vp build"; preview "vite preview" becomes "vp preview". eslint to vp lint and prettier to vp fmt only if those optional migrations run. bunx forms preserved (bunx --bun vite build becomes bunx --bun vp build).

vite.config.ts: the defineConfig import from "vite" is rewritten to "vite-plus" ONLY in config entry files; app source keeps vite imports which resolve through the alias. Tool-specific configs merge into vite.config.ts blocks: lint{}, fmt{}, staged{}, pack{}.

tsconfig: migration runs ts5to6 fixBaseUrl because tsgolint does not support baseUrl. remindit-pwa tsconfig.app.json uses paths WITHOUT baseUrl so this is a no-op.

index.html is NOT touched. No vitest imports exist in this repo so no source rewrites happen. Optional setup actions: git hook dispatcher (.vite-hooks/pre-commit plus core.hooksPath) is DEFAULT in non-interactive mode, use --no-hooks to skip; AGENTS.md/editor files only via --agent/--editor flags; ESLint/Prettier migration is opt-in; nvmrc conversion not applicable (no .nvmrc present).

In remindit-app-pwa, rstest tests for stores MUST import submodules directly (e.g. `@/stores/user`) and NOT the `@/stores` barrel — the barrel runs `initStores` + a dev logger as a side effect that breaks isolated tests. The global test environment is happy-dom (set via testEnvironment: "happy-dom" in rstest.config.ts), so `localStorage` and `crypto.randomUUID()` are available without extra setup. Use `resetStores` from tests/fixtures/reset.ts with `beforeEach(resetStores)` to clear stores + localStorage between tests.

RESEARCH 3/4 - gotchas for remindit-pwa stack under vite+. Post-migration behavior: deps reinstalled once to refresh lockfile (nonzero exit if install fails), warns on Rolldown-incompatible patterns like manualChunks (not used here), oxfmt formats changed files but SKIPS formatting while Prettier still present. Migration is idempotent.

Tailwind v4 (@tailwindcss/vite ^4): no open compatibility issues in voidzero-dev/vite-plus GitHub repo; already proven under Vite 8 Rolldown in this project, plugin behavior unchanged. CSS-first tokens in src/index.css untouched by migration.

React 19 + @vitejs/plugin-react ^6: already working under Vite 8, migrate makes no framework changes. Optional perf: wrap plugins in lazyPlugins(() => [react(), tailwindcss()]) so vp lint/fmt/check skip loading them during metadata-only config loads.

Formatter trap: prettier-plugin-tailwindcss class sorting. Oxfmt has native sortTailwindcss support but had closed diffs vs Prettier on Tailwind v4 @theme/@theme inline colors (oxc issue 25109). Keep Prettier initially if formatting parity matters; cut over to oxfmt deliberately later.

Linter trap: eslint.config.js exempts generated src/components/ui from several rules; Oxlint migration will not translate custom overrides one-to-one. Oxlint covers react-hooks and react-refresh equivalents; JS plugins escape hatch exists. Do ESLint-to-Oxlint cutover as a separate deliberate step.

Centralized dotenv in a Bun monorepo (Next/Payload admin + Astro web + Playwright e2e): root .env is NOT auto-loaded by subprocesses. `bunx --bun` disables Bun's .env auto-loading entirely. Next sets NODE_ENV itself so dotenv cannot override it (only affects non-Next contexts like payload CLI). Astro's config file (.mjs) does not read .env automatically, use Vite's loadEnv or feed env through a regeneration step. Pattern that works: each consumer calls dotenv.config({ path: path.resolve(<workspace>, '../.env') }) explicitly; a config.toml→JSON watcher reads root .env and overrides site.baseUrl, chained into dev/build scripts (node scripts/... && astro dev) so the committed generated JSON picks up env values and can be gitignored.

Validating a PWA manifest with the chrome-devtools MCP (this project's setup uses Google Chrome launched with --remote-debugging-pipe, so there is NO TCP debug port — curl http://localhost:PORT/json is unavailable and CDP Page.getAppManifest cannot be called directly). To capture what Chrome's Application>Manifest panel would report, replicate its checks IN-PAGE via chrome-devtools_evaluate_script: fetch('/manifest.webmanifest'), parse, then (a) verify required fields (name/short_name, start_url, display, background_color, theme_color, icons), (b) confirm a 192px and 512px icon exist, (c) fetch each icon and decode via `new Image()` checking naturalWidth===naturalHeight (square) and HTTP 200, (d) resolve start_url/scope against location.origin for same-origin, (e) list console messages with types error/warn/info/issue. This reproduces Chrome's installability/Manifest errors without the literal panel UI.

Swarm coordination pattern that worked for tooling migrations (vite->vite+): 3 sequential cells (research -> migrate -> independent verify) with research findings injected into the migrate worker's shared_context. vp migrate gotchas discovered: it force-applies Oxlint/Oxfmt cutover even WITHOUT --full and rewrites eslint-disable comments in src files OUTSIDE the worker's file scope - revert with git restore and defer lint/format cutover deliberately. Also: swarm_complete consistently fails with "Missing required parameters: start_time" schema bug in this environment; coordinators must close cells manually via hive_close after review. sqlite SQLITE_BUSY errors on hive/swarmmail tools are transient - retry once.

In the remindit-app-pwa repo, unit tests for the nanostores store layer follow these conventions (verified against tests/stores/history.test.ts): (1) import submodules directly, NOT the `@/stores` barrel, because the barrel runs initStores + a dev logger as a side effect; (2) happy-dom is configured globally (no per-file setup needed for localStorage/crypto.randomUUID); (3) reset between tests via `beforeEach(resetStores)` from `tests/fixtures/reset.ts`, which clears all stores + localStorage; (4) seed deterministic data by calling `.set()` directly on `$categories`/`$catalog`/`$list`. The derived selectors in src/stores/selectors.ts preserve $categories order: $itemsByCategory groups active list entries under their category in $categories order and excludes categories with no entries; $activeCategoryIds = group category ids in that order; $listCount = list length; $checkedCount = checked entries. Gotcha: when writing tests, the seed $categories order must match the asserted group order, otherwise assertions about ordering ($activeCategoryIds) will fail.

In this repo's swarm setup, the swarm_review tool diffs the working file against a stale snapshot (not HEAD), producing huge misleading diffs. Always verify actual changes with `git diff HEAD -- <file>` before approving. Confirmed during the theme-toggle epic where globals.css showed a 400-line diff in review but was only +4 lines vs HEAD.

RESEARCH 4/4 - commands, sequence, rollback for vite+ migration of remindit-pwa.

COMMANDS: built-ins cannot be overridden. vp dev/build/test always run the built-in tools; vp run <script> (alias vpr) runs package.json scripts. bun run dev/build keep working because scripts remain in package.json. IMPORTANT: vp build does NOT typecheck; vp check typecheck uses tsgolint (TypeScript 7 Go port), NOT tsc. Must keep "build": "tsc -b && vp build" since tsc -b is the real type gate for this repo (bare tsc --noEmit on files:[] root verifies nothing per AGENTS.md).

RECOMMENDED SEQUENCE: 0) clean git tree, feature branch. 1) vp upgrade (latest CLI migration rules). 2) confirm Vite 8+ (project already ^8). 3) vp migrate --no-interactive (add --no-hooks to skip hook dispatcher; skip agent/editor flags). 4) review diffs: package.json (vite-plus dep, overrides.vite alias, direct vite edge, script rewrites) and vite.config.ts defineConfig import. 5) verify: bun install, bun run build (tsc -b && vp build), bun run dev, then vp check. 6) defer ESLint/Prettier to Oxlint/Oxfmt cutover as separate deliberate step to isolate risk.

ROLLBACK: all edits are working-tree files (package.json, bun.lock, vite.config.ts, maybe hooks/AGENTS.md). Rollback = git restore . && git clean -fd on branch, then bun install. Disable hooks via vp hooks disable or restore core.hooksPath. Remove global tool entirely with vp implode. If install fails mid-migrate the command exits nonzero leaving partial changes; git is the safety net.

In the remindit-app-pwa (Rsbuild + React 19 + Bun) project: the `bun run lint` command referenced in AGENTS.md does NOT exist as an npm script. Use `bunx @biomejs/biome check src/...` (or `biome lint`) instead. Also `@nanostores/logger` v1.1 exports `logger({ Name: store })` (object map), NOT `logStore`. And `@nanostores/persistent` `persistentJSON<T>(name, initial)` handles JSON object/array persistence with no manual encode/decode. `import.meta.env` is not typed by default (no Rsbuild client types in tsconfig), so augment `interface ImportMeta` via `declare global` or use `import.meta.env?.DEV` with a cast. Rsbuild/Rspack does resolve JSON imports from outside `src/` (e.g. `../../docs/samples/*.json`), so seeding stores by importing a sample JSON file works.

Payload CMS + SQLite: when a collection is removed from payload.config.ts, the dev-server auto-sync will NOT drop orphaned tables or their FK columns from join tables like payload_locked_documents_rels. Cleanup must be done manually with sqlite3 CLI. Key gotcha: ALTER TABLE ... DROP COLUMN fails with "unknown column in foreign key definition" when the column is used in a FK constraint (even with foreign_keys=OFF), so the table must be recreated (CREATE new, copy data, DROP old, RENAME) and indexes recreated manually. Also: DROP COLUMN requires dropping any dedicated indexes on the column first. Verification: PRAGMA integrity_check, check sqlite_master for orphan tables, PRAGMA table_info on join tables. Backup db first: sqlite3 hct.db '.backup hct.db.bak'.
